text:
Darren Raddysh, a Toronto kid who went undrafted and worked his way up through the AHL, came home this season after 249 games in Tampa and walked straight into a 24-minute role. He's played more than 29 minutes in a game and averages 23:49, and Yahoo Sports ran a piece asking whether even he is surprised by how Jim Hiller has used him.

The points are fine, 14 in 23 with eight on the power play. The goals aren't: one on 52 shots, 1.9% against the 7% our range expects. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot more than almost any defenseman last season (99th percentile), so a man with a 98 mph shot should not stay stuck at one.

The harder question is the team around him. Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.6 wins last season, 15th among defensemen, but noted he played with very strong teammates in Tampa. In Toronto, the Leafs have 47% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about what they manage without him, and they've won one of his last ten games.
